data.name: Maneesh
data.gender_notes: Maneesh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Maneesh is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Manas', meaning mind, and 'Ish', meaning God. The name Maneesh signifies the Moon God. The name Maneesh carries the meaning “Moon God” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Maneesh usually hope their child will grow to embody moon god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Maneesh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Moon God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Maneesh total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

historical_references.reference: Mahabharata, an ancient Sanskrit epic that is one of the two major sources for Hindu mythology and Indian philosophy. In this epic, Maneesh is mentioned as the name of a sage who was a disciple of the sage Vyasa, the author of the Mahabharata.

Another reference to Maneesh can be found in the Puranic texts, specifically in the Agni Purana. Here, Maneesh is mentioned as one of the 21 Prajaapatis or celestial beings who were born from the mind of Brahma, the creator god in Hinduism.
